title: Tenali Raman and the Well of Truth

full_text:
A wealthy merchant of Vijayanagara named Govinda Chetty was burgled of a brass pot containing five hundred gold mohurs. The theft had occurred without any broken locks, indicating that someone familiar with the household was responsible.
Govinda approached Tenali Raman, weeping and pleading for assistance.

Tenali investigated the merchant’s mansion quietly. He noticed that the household had an ancient, disused stone well in the rear courtyard, covered with heavy timber planks. Tenali observed that the moss around the well rim was freshly scratched and disturbed.
Suspecting that the thief had hidden the heavy pot inside the well rather than risking carrying it through the city gates, Tenali devised a psychological trap.

In the presence of all five servants and relatives, Tenali solemnly announced:
'Govinda Chetty, the theft of thy gold is an omen. This evening at twilight, the Chief Astrologer and I shall perform the ancient Rite of the Sacred Well. We shall light seventy-seven oil lamps around the rim, invoke the spirits of truth, and lower a consecrated brass hook into the water. If the stolen gold is inside, the spirits will bring it to the surface before the entire neighborhood!'

The suspects listened with wide eyes.
Tenali and Govinda then left the courtyard, pretending to go to the bazaar to purchase ceremonial incense and camphor.
Instead, Tenali and four armed guards hid behind the high brick wall of the adjoining stable.

Within two hours, just as dusk fell, one of the merchant’s trusted grooms, a youth named Somu, crept into the courtyard looking around nervously.
Believing that the 'spirits of truth' would expose him during the announced ritual, Somu hurriedly pulled away the timber planks, tied a rope around his waist, lowered himself into the well, and retrieved the heavy brass pot of gold from an underwater stone niche!

As soon as Somu climbed out onto the courtyard paving stones with the dripping pot of gold in his hands, Tenali and the guards stepped out of the shadows with lanterns!

Somu dropped the pot, the gold coins clattered across the stone floor, and he fell prostrate in terror.
'Forgive me, master!' he sobbed. 'I thought the spirits would strike me dead during the ritual!'

Tenali smiled:
'The only spirit at work here, Somu, was the spirit of thy own guilty conscience!'
The gold was restored to the grateful merchant, Somu was sentenced to community service, and Tenali demonstrated that understanding human psychology is the sharpest tool of justice.
moral: Guilt makes a thief anticipate discovery; a subtle hint causes criminals to expose their own hidden loot.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Thieves and the Well"?
options: Wit and humor triumph over arrogance and power
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.

the ability to judge well and understand the truth

Imagine an alternate peaceful ending or a new creative adventure for these characters.
